status.en: 25 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 92% more than the week before, most of them in Baghdad, Sulaymaniyah and Diyala.
status.nb: 25 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 92 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Baghdad, Sulaymaniyah og Diyala.

summary.en: Iraqi security forces have taken control of three checkpoints in Jurf al-Sakhar and reopened the Karbala road while Kataib Hezbollah begins a phased withdrawal from the area. The government and Egypt have agreed to scrap visa requirements and signed tax and cooperation deals, and the Iraqi prime minister is preparing a Cairo visit to deepen economic ties. Oil thefts have been reported across all governorates with estimated losses of $150 billion, and a gas pipeline fire at the Hartha power station near Basra killed at least four people and injured dozens. The UCDP recorded 396 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Irakiske sikkerhetsstyrker har tatt kontroll over tre kontrollposter i Jurf al-Sakhar og gjenåpnet Karbala-veien mens Kataib Hezbollah begynner en trinnvis tilbaketrekning fra området. Regjeringen og Egypt har blitt enige om å avskaffe visumkrav og har signert skatte‑ og samarbeidsavtaler, og Iraks statsminister forbereder et besøk i Kairo for å styrke de økonomiske båndene. Oljetap er rapportert i alle governorater med anslåtte tap på $150 milliarder, og en gassledningsbrann ved Hartha kraftstasjon nær Basra drepte minst fire personer og såret flere titalls. UCDP registrerte 396 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.extract: The Iraqi conflict is a series of violent events that began with the 2003 American-led invasion of Iraq and deposition of Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein, followed by a series of conflicts including the protracted Iraq War (2003–2011), the Iraqi insurgency (2011–2013), the War in Iraq (2013–2017), and most recently, the small-scale Islamic State insurgency in 4 provinces located in Northern Iraq since 2017.
